rv.q: Like any great artistic piece, Witch is beautiful and brave, but above all, Witch asks us to think deeply about what it means to have hope, or stop having hope, in a world that isn’t always fair and gets a little more complicated every day.
In this sharp adaptation of a little-known Jacobean drama, the playwright has injected new life into an old story from four centuries ago.
Silverman’s script is wise in its sharp tongue and makes a statement on the general apathy many feel every day.
The arias are each a lovely insight into the character and Carson stages each to give the actor a literal moment in the spotlight.
“Witch” is a treasure and one of the best shows I’ve seen all year.
Devon Carson’s masterful direction of Witch for The Artistic Home is a stunning theatrical event that demands to be seen.
